This paper proposes MO-SAC-B, a multi-objective deep reinforcement learning framework that integrates behavioral science theory into the scheduling optimization process. We first construct a behavior-driven discrete-event simulation environment that encodes prospect-theoretic waiting disutility, nonlinear patience decay, and behaviorally calibrated no-show and abandonment dynamics.
